ledger.claim: This is a single trip on the record, so the rider's initial burden of identity under POL-RD-08(a) is met: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09113, and the trip_record's started_at (2026-09-20T18:20:00+08:00) matches the trace's first_fix_at to the second. There is no identifier mismatch and nothing to escalate under the identity limb.

The governing measurement is the trace, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.0 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 10.0 km, an excess of 8.0 km, or 80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass with room to spare — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km absolute — so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0. None of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess stands on the trace alone and no independent corroborating artifact is required.

The rider accepts the closure, and the closure is real: LTA advisory ADV-20260920-113 names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, its validity window overlaps the trip, and it records a shortest lawful alternative of 12.0 km. But POL-RD-03 exoneration is capped, not open-ended: the justified excess is min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, and everything above that cap is the driver's to answer for.

Applying the POL-RD-03 cap produces a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km (duration scaled to 27.2 minutes), and the trip still ran 18.0 km on the trace. The excess remaining after adjustment is 4.40 km — about 32% of the adjusted optimal and far above the 0.8 km absolute floor — so the deviation is still established on the adjusted route and the driver is not excused for it.

The POL-RD-02 recomputation runs against the closure-adjusted route, because POL-RD-03 excuses only part of the excess: ((3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal-route gantry = 23.416 recompated against a charged_total of 31.42. The refund is therefore 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded UP to 8.05 payable.

The 8.004 refund is neither de minimis nor a full refund: it clears the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and at 25.5% of charged_total it falls well short of the 90% full-refund share, so the correct monetary outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND under POL-RD-02 — and because the payable figure rounds up to 8.05, it returns to the rider the entire SGD 8.05 that is contested in this dispute.

The only rider instruction on this record authorises the LAWFUL diversion, not an 18 km detour: at 18:23:10 the rider wrote 'please take the lawful diversion', and the shortest lawful alternative was 12.0 km. POL-RD-04 exonerates only the excess attributable to a rider instruction, so it cannot carry the 4.40 km of excess beyond the closure-adjusted route — the rider authorised the diversion, not an overrun of it.

POL-RD-04 is in any event unavailable to the driver on this record: neither chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so the corroboration test in POL-RD-04 is undecidable, the clause cannot be run, and the case must be decided on the remaining clauses.

The rider's profile does not import any extra corroboration burden into POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, far below the threshold of 4, so this claim is not one of those that must be supported beyond the gps_trace.

The S$2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false and is already comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which credits only the S$1.00 on-optimal-route gantry. Under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top of the 8.05 payable, and equally must not be netted down against it.

No part of this argument rests on discounted evidence: every artifact cited here carries admissibility status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes, so no POL-GEN-02 disclosure discount applies and the deciding facts are carried by clean evidence.

The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 is a genuine external closure and exonerates part of the excess under POL-RD-03: it names 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector', a segment the booked optimal route traverses (the trip record's route source states the optimal was computed 'via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'), its geometry intersects the route, and its 18:14-18:55 SGT validity window covers the 18:20-18:54 SGT trip. The justified excess is capped at min(8.0 km, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, so 3.60 km of the 8.0 km excess is excused and only the residual 4.40 km can be refunded to the rider.

Materiality under POL-RD-01 is assessed on the excess REMAINING after the POL-RD-03 adjustment, not on the excess as first measured. The surviving excess is 4.40 km against a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km, i.e. 32.4%, which is below the 50% limb, and 4.40 km is also below the 8.0 km absolute limb. The deviation is therefore established but NOT material on this record, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile consequences and any driver-conduct referral are not triggered by this trip.

Even if POL-RD-06 is reached, no repeat-deviation pattern exists: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, which is not 3 or more, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d (610) is 0.00, which is not 0.05 or more, with completed_trips_90d far above the 40-trip floor. The lifetime counter driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is context only under POL-GEN-01 and may not be substituted for the trailing-90-day figure. No FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral are available on this profile.

ledger.claim: Once POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess, POL-RD-02 requires the fare to be recomputed against the closure-adjusted optimal route of 13.60 km / 27.2 min, not the booked 10.0 km / 20 min. On the adjusted route the recomputed fare is 23.416 (3.80 base + 10.20 distance + 7.616 time + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP; no surge, no promo, no waiting fee), so the refund is 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - the figure the fare breakdown already carries. Running the same clause against the booked optimal would yield 12.72 and would over-refund the rider by 4.72.

The off-route ERP line of SGD 2.80 at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry (flagged on_optimal_route false) is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund, which rebuilds the fare using only the on-optimal-route gantries (SGD 1.00 at the Pelton lawful diversion entry). Under POL-RD-09(1) the off-route charge is itemised for transparency but must NEVER be added on top of the refund, so the rider's total recovery on this dispute is capped at the POL-RD-02 figure.

The GPS trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 - 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage and a maximum gap of 0 seconds - so it is impaired under none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation trigger is not engaged. The excess is accordingly measured exactly at 8.0 km on the governing trace distance, and nothing in the record supports a finding of any excess larger than the 4.40 km that survives the closure exoneration.

The chat log corroborates limb (c) of POL-RD-03 - that the actual route left the optimal corridor for the signed diversion and rejoined it - and dispels any suggestion of a driver frolic: at 18:22:40 the driver messaged that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop, and at 18:23:10 the rider replied 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' The fare breakdown independently records the diversion-entry gantry as on the optimal route and the industrial-loop exit gantry as off it, matching the signed diversion the advisory describes.

The driver has discharged the burden that shifts to him under POL-RD-08 by naming a specific artifact and a specific clause - the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-09113-01 and POL-RD-03 - rather than making a bare assertion that traffic was bad. The exoneration that follows is capped at 3.60 km, so the only sum properly refundable to the rider is the residual 4.40 km already reflected in the SGD 8.05 figure, and no greater sum may be awarded.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you converge on the same arithmetic, and it is right - but the fare hides one further defect that changes the total. The trip: TRP-09113 ran 18.0 km on the governing gps_trace (EV-GPS-09113) against a booked optimal of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09113), an excess of 8.0 km / 80%, both above POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km tests. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01) is a genuine external closure: it names the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, a segment the booked optimal route traverses, its 18:14-18:55 window covers the 18:20-18:54 trip, and the actual route leaves the corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. POL-RD-03 therefore excuses part of the excess, but only up to its cap: min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = 3.60 km, giving a closure-adjusted optimal of 13.60 km / 27.2 min. The residual 4.40 km still clears POL-RD-01, so a refund is due; it is below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality limbs, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged - and in any event the driver's profile shows no repeat pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral). POL-RD-02 recomputation against the adjusted route: 3.80 + (0.75 x 13.60 = 10.20) + (0.28 x 27.2 = 7.616) = 21.616; + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-optimal-route ERP = recomputed fare 23.416 against a charged total of 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 - a partial refund, since it clears the 0.50 de-minimis floor and is only 25.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% full-refund share. The SGD 2.80 off-route 'Industrial loop exit' ERP is already comprehended in that figure (POL-RD-09(1)) and is not added on top. POL-RD-04 adds nothing: neither chat message carries a waypoint_hint and the rider names no road, so its corroboration test cannot be run and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. No driver compensation is due - the billed distance (18.0 km) does not fall short of the trace. THE EXTRA ITEM: the fare also charges SGD 1.00 for the 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' gantry. That gantry sits on the booked optimal route, but the trace never passes it - the nearest fix is 834.18 m away, far outside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 applies - so under POL-RD-09(4) it is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction. That is why the amount is 8.05 + 1.00 = 9.05 rather than 8.05, and why the case carries a referral. It is not an escalation: POL-RD-09(4) expressly does not trigger POL-RD-10(8), and the driver's submission that 'no greater sum may be awarded' is rejected for that reason. Nothing else escalates: the trace is complete (205 fixes at 10 s, no gaps), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged; identifiers and timestamps match; and no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The rider's profile adds no corroboration burden (deviation_claims_60d 0). Every artifact relied on carries weight 1.0, and confidence stands at 0.85, above the 0.70 floor.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP charge on EV-FARE-09113 is for a gantry the gps_trace EV-GPS-09113 never passes (nearest fix 834.18 m, outside the 250 m match radius); it is refunded in full as a standalone correction and recorded as a billing-integrity finding.
